title: Random Bots In The Lobby
description: The host can fill a lobby with random bots without a password: an 'Add random bot' button, a 'Fill empty seats with random bots' button, a 'Random bot' badge in the seat list and a 'Remove bot' action. A random bot plays legal moves at random inside the game server (no extra process, no model), so a table can be tested alone or with friends. Before, the only 'Add Bot' was the MLP bot, which needs a server bot password and a model service, so nobody could add one. The before shots were taken on the base commit (unified-latest-2026-10-08) with TI4_SHOT_PREFIX=before and are committed as PNGs; the after shots are regenerated by npm run screenshots -- AV. Synthetic: the real lobby components against a mocked server, not a live game.

shots.heading: Before: the host cannot add a bot
shots.caption: Four seats, two taken. Open seats read 'Available' and offer nothing: the MLP 'Add Bot' appears only when the server runs the bot service.

shots.heading: After: two buttons above the seat list
shots.caption: 'Add random bot' seats one bot in the first open seat, 'Fill empty seats with random bots' takes every open seat. Neither asks for a password; the host's own session authorises it.

shots.heading: Before: a bot looks like any player
shots.caption: A bot seat, as the mocked server would report it, has no label and shows a Connected dot.

shots.heading: After: one random bot seated
shots.caption: The seat reads 'Random bot 1' with a 'Random bot' badge and 'Plays itself' instead of a connection state; it is ready from the start. The host can still add more or fill.

shots.heading: Before: filled lobby
shots.caption: Every seat taken, no hint which are bots.

shots.heading: After: every open seat filled
shots.caption: One click filled the table. The add and fill buttons disappear because no seat is open; Start waits only for the people.

shots.heading: Before: removing a seat
shots.caption: The host's remove (x) button exists for any non-host seat; the seat opens and nothing else changes.

shots.heading: After: 'Remove bot' frees the seat
shots.caption: The button is labelled 'Remove bot at position 3' for a bot; the seat opens again and the add and fill buttons return. A re-added bot takes the first unused name.

shots.heading: Before (phone): open seats
shots.caption: 390 px wide. Open seats only say 'Available'.

shots.heading: After (phone): stacked, touch sized buttons
shots.caption: The two buttons wrap onto their own rows, are at least 44 px tall and never overflow the screen; the hint below says what random bots do.

shots.heading: After (phone): filled with bots
shots.caption: The badges wrap under the name, the remove button stays reachable, and the page does not scroll sideways (asserted).

shots.heading: Before: another player's view
shots.caption: Guests see the seats and their state.

shots.heading: After: guests see the badges, never the buttons
shots.caption: Only the host gets 'Add random bot' and 'Fill'. Everyone sees which seats are random bots.

shots.heading: Older server (no bot_kinds)
shots.caption: A server that predates random bots does not list bot kinds.

shots.heading: After: older server, same lobby
shots.caption: No bot kinds in the lobby response means no random bot buttons: the client never offers what the server cannot do.

shots.heading: Before: server with the MLP service
shots.caption: Per-seat 'Add Bot' with a password dialog, as before.

shots.heading: After: both bot kinds
shots.caption: The MLP 'Add Bot' per seat is untouched; the random bot buttons sit above the list.
